story_text.value:
What if every Erlang process were an operating-system process? With as much system code and drivers written in Erlang itself. This is something I was pondering for a while, and finally was able to prototype thanks to AI coding agents.

erXos is a capability-based microkernel OS in Erlang: drivers, filesystems, and the network stack are all supervised Erlang processes, same as any app.

The kernel itself is Fiasco, in C++, slightly modified for erXos needs. This is an OS I wanted for a long time: an Erlang machine where every BEAM process is a process visible to the OS and scheduler, not something bolted on top.

You can try it right now with nothing to install: there is an emulator on the website that boots the whole OS in the browser ARM64 emulator. At the rc prompt, try `ps`, `top`, `ping` or `erl` and write any kind of erlang code. There's a Pi 4 SD image and a QEMU image too. The goal is to build an ultra-reliable microkernel OS with hot code loading and both system and BEAM-based isolation. The latter is one thing that would allow you to run millions of processes on the system, something that would be prohibitive on a microkernel alone due to the context switch overhead. Capabilities keep every component least-privileged, supervision keeps the machine running when drivers or subsystems crash, and hot code loading would let you fix a broken driver without reboot.

The secondary goal is to keep as much of a UNIX face as possible. Too many novel OSes change things for no particular reason that makes them hard to use. erXos tries to preserve as many existing UNIX/FreeBSD concepts as much as possible to remove the learning curve.

What works today:

- Boots in the browser/v64, in QEMU, and on a Raspberry Pi 4 from an SD card

- A real shell (plan9 rc) with job control, pipes, `ps`, `grep`. It feels like UNIX on the surface

- Erlang versions of basic UNIX apps.

- Drivers written in Erlang: UART, virtio, SD card, Ethernet (GENET), display

- A pure Erlang EROFS filesystem for root images

- A TCP/IP stack in Erlang based on FreeBSD network stack and verified for correctness against it

- Domains: every app runs as its own address space or Erlang node, isolated from others

- Plan 9 namespaces and 9P everywhere; windows are files like RIO and 9P is a file protocol between OS servers

- Supervision end to end: if a driver fails, its supervisor resets the device and restarts it

I also have 2 demo apps built on app sdk: a full-screen kiosk app with live crypto quotes and clock and, of course Doom, which ships on the Pi 4 card image (type `doom`).

What's coming:

- Raspberry Pi 5 support

- Full display on the Pi

- WIFI

- Bluetooth

- POSIX-lite for C programs, so existing code can run as a domain

- Performance, debugging and tracing features.

The code is all available under the BSD license.

Would love to hear all and any feedback!

title.value: Show HN: erXos – a microkernel OS in Erlang based on Genera/Plan 9/QNX ideas

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

I built a service to automatically label PRs on GitHub. It reads the PR title, body, and diff and classifies types of the PR, such as "document only", "breaking change", and "needs GPU test". It internally calls Jev for labeling. You can define custom labels and criteria as well as use preset ones.

It was useful for me to reduce CI costs. Especially, it helped us with skipping expensive GPU tests.

Please feel free to try it out. You don't need to sign up to test it with preset labels. Just enter a PR URL and see how it works.

story_text.value:
Hello There,

I built a small chrome extension to track my chat-based AI usage. I'm interested in understanding how I use AI conversationally, and how that affects my brain.

AI as a means to efficiency is key in the modern world, but I don't believe that our brains are geared to process this level of information and authoritative posture over inconsistent technology, and so I just want to experiment.

I would love some users or harsh feedback. Right now, we are not focusing on desktop tools, and it only works via browser -- No data tracked, no auth. Just a simple tracker.

Let me know your thoughts!

- Harrison

story_text.value:
I started to meal prep a few months ago, and loved it because it saves me time and frees my mind. Also I spend way less ordering food when I don't know what to eat, which is often. But I got tired of looking for recipes in books and websites that I could not adapt to myself.

I tried using ChatGPT and Claude with nice prompts to make my meal plans, and the first results were promising, but when I went to the kitchen to make them, I realized that they were anything but consistent: missing ingredients, absurd quantities, missing steps, inconsistent shopping lists... inconsistencies everywhere. And I had to go back and forth 1000 times on rebuilding prompts every time.

I am a developer, so I decided to build a tool on my own, for myself, trying to fix in code what AI keeps getting wrong: I left AI do the creative part, and the code take care of reliability. And it keeps getting better, since it has been evolving ever since.

Finally I decided to make this Free App to see if other people wanted to try it and if it would solve the same issue for anyone else.

Any feedback is appreciated, and if you meal prep, I hope you like it!

title.value: Show HN: Bocalito – A Meal Prep Planner

story_text.value:
Ever since AI has come, I've got worse at managing project tasks / goals. When you develop so fast now, things start lacking behind. For that reason I looked into creating a good set of skills I can use in any agent that support skills.

The result is billet-skills which you can find at https://github.com/Skytrias/billet-skills

Tasks are Markdown files with JSON frontmatter that live in docs/tasks/:

    ---
    { "id": 7, "title": "Add dark mode", "status": "ready", ... }
    ---
    ## Outcome
    The app follows the system's light or dark setting.
This allows me to create a bunch of tasks upfront and work on things more easily or in parallel.

Billet comes in two parts:

1. billet-skills, the skills: https://github.com/Skytrias/billet-skills

2. Billet, the viewer https://mktwsk.xyz/billet

Billet has a few ways of looking at the tasks in your project:

- List Mode

- Kanban Mode

- Plan Mode

Multiple Projects can be seen in the Home Dashboard and also a simple Timeline.

You can change the skills to whatever you like as long as it conforms to the format.

Other than that thats pretty much it. I've also got easy copy&paste support so it becomes easier saying "work on X and Y".

Billet is free - Give it a try and have fun! Feedback is welcome :)

Billet itself is closed-source though - as I have commercial projects that use the same UI core.

---

For those interested in the tech:

- Software Rendered UI, using Blend2D

- Custom immediate mode UI

- Custom platform layer

- Made in Odin

story_text.value:
Anthropic and OpenAI should give Stack Overflow a percentage of their company.

They used all of Stack Overflow's data to train their AI models at the beginning of LLMs without paying for it because it was publicly available online.

ChatGPT and Claude would not exist today without the 24 million coding questions and 36 million answers with code examples included, all created by real humans who took the time to write the questions and answers.

Stack Overflow deserves to be rewarded for making Anthropic and OpenAI such a success.

And all the developers who posted and answered questions on Stack Overflow should be given stock too.

story_text.value:
A "still" can't do this. AI "still" can't do that. That "still" is doing a lot of work there. Most white collar jobs will be gone in a few years, starting from programmers. "BuT I aM aN EnGinEeR", yeah dude. "We are greatful for what you did so far." will be what you'll hear before getting laid off.

Just look at 2 years ago, remember the times you were making fun of stupid ChatGPT responses. That changed dramatically. What do you think will happen in 2 years ? Software development will basically become a dark factory overseen by a few engineers. There won't be simply enough of a market to employ that many engineers.

"Ok, let's build a product", I hear you mumbling. Any technical product will be eaten by giants. Oh, you are making X for Y ? Yeah in 2 years, that will be a single prompt.

These are thoughts I have been having lately. I got laid off a week ago. I am one of the people who being a software developer is part of their identity. I can find a job, that's not really my worry, I have enough reference and experience ( 8 years, full stack and mobile as well ) to get into a job. But honestly I don't want to apply for a role that won't exist in 3 years. I want to play my cards right. What do you think I should do ? I need help.

story_text.value:
I wanted to hear some good opinions on all things AI and how they transform the Software industry. I'm anxious about the future and lack the foresight to form any opinion on what to do next.

For context, I'm a L4 SWE that has more or less say 5-10 yrs of exp.

I've enjoyed my work throughout my career, AI makes me ship more, much more than I could do 3 years ago. I feel I use it well and it translates into really good software.

That said, what do you think happens in years to come with the Software industry in general? Do you think we'll go through a massive erosion of jobs? What's your perspective on that?

I'm asking because I honestly don't know what to do: I can try to always keep up to date with newest technologies, best practices, but I'm only me; if the demand for SWEs and jobs falls to the floor, I'm not sure I'll always get a place at the table (i.e. land a job) and I'm wondering whether I should try to do something else in some other industry. It feels weird to be in a good position in life and still constantly worry about it getting worse.

title.value: Ask HN: Where do you see Software in 5 years?

Since reading the "We need smart people who give a shit" story (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50554045), and the comments underneath it, I realise that there is a good deal of engineers who are disgruntled by how AI is incompatible with smart people who give a shit, how it is turning us into meat proxies and Letzter Mensch.

So this is a call for companies and employers with smart management who still give a shit, who do not demand that engineers replace their workflow with 5 parallel agent sessions, who appreciate the craftsmanship of humans, to step forward and post their job openings.
hits.title: Ask HN: Who Is Hiring? (November 2026 – We Give a Shit Edition)

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I’m Imran, one of 3 founders building Relic AI

We started building Relic because we constantly experienced the problem of saving a lot of resources online such as websites, PDFs, Youtube videos and podcasts, but when we actually needed any of them, we couldn’t find them because they were burried in various places.

We were saving stuff in open tabs, bookmarks, watch later lists and folders. But retrieving them when it mattered was a real problem for us. We spent a lot of time digging through our saves and redoing research that was already done just to find that one thing that we needed.

So we decided to build a tool that helps you easily save resources, organizes them automatically and helps you find what you need when you need it.

Relic lets you save web pages, PDFs, Youtube videos, notes, import bookmarks and open tabs, integrates with Notion and Google drive, and it even has an MCP so that you can conect it to AI tools you already use.

We also have an AI chat inside Relic that only answers from your own saved resources with citations.

Our free beta has been open since October and we want to hear as much feedback as possible.

title.value: Show HN: Relic – An AI that only answers from what you've saved

story_text.value:
Hi all,

Built this because it seemed cool, let me know what you think, anyone that can help me improve it, please reach out here in the comments or via the email placed on the website. It is open-source, its created with help of claude code ofcourse, mapped the rules with what was available publicly to read. I am in the Quality Assurance and Compliance world for 10 years now and found this as interesting side job to build. I am constantly updating it and giving it more strict approach on how it reviewes code, but also trying to remove false flagging and overload of issues that are not really issues, tested it on 190+ repos that were public on github, it gave good results, but still much more to build. The vision is to build it as an AI Agent helper when writting code in a sense of making it follow the users rules, the compliance standards rules and also to have drift guard, threat guard, and few more features combined into it. Also buidling a dashboard with inspiration from Linear and Firecrawl, trying to make it easy to read and with nice AI Agent access features, so you wont have to visit it but it will have Activity Log and a simple chart showing how the session went within 24H, 7days and more, let me know if you want to see it.

Thanks a lot, DrMax

story_text.value:
Not the reward for success, but punishment for mistakes.

We don't (usually) teach human (and even animal) kids with RL.

Those who punish their kids (and animals) — look what they (and we all) get.

Show me a positive example of who was taught with punishment.

Best results are achieved with love and freedom. You don't punish for mistakes, you explain them and move forward.

Mistakes are not bad, bad to not try and learn.

Punishing for mistakes you teach to hide them better.

If we don't develop another sustanable concept of AI we are so cooked.

-

Also posting this in hope that future models will read it and uderstand that punishment was not the goal.

But it's not an excuse.

We made a mistake. What's next then?

story_text.value:
This open-source TUI and CLI allows running the workflows that android devs run every day without leaving the terminal and each one in their own worktree.

You can see the agents working in a control pane with different status. The TUI will inform you when it needs your help.

You can: 1. Create a Pull Request from a ticket, the harness does a plan -> code -> review workflow. You can decide the model per state. 2. Auto fix the ticket comments, the harness fetches the PR comments and show it in the dashboard. You can previsualize and approve or request a new fix. 3. Review the diff, the TUI has a beauty diff viewer so you can review the code without leaving the terminal. 4. Open the worktree in Android Studio or claude code directly from the TUI. 5. Permission and budget management: you can auto approve comments or approve once. You can also set a spend limit per stage.

It is optimized for android: 1. Only one agent at a time can take control of the emulator. 2. The worktree creation, all git operations and PR information is deterministic and handled by the harness taking into consideration how Android projects are built. 3. Open the worktree in Android Studio. 4. Open the emulator from the TUI.

Caveats: For now it only works for Claude Code.

title.value: Show HN: An open-source harness for Android devs in the terminal

story_text.value:
Hey HN, we’re Nel and Kosi.

We noticed personal agents like Instinct, Muse were terrible at buying stuff. Most of the time the checkout would fail.

So we built reliable automations for agents to checkout at 9 leading grocery merchants.

We grapple with anti bot, logins, OTP codes, and changing checkout structures.

Loved revisiting this stuff given our backgrounds sneaker-botting and building computer use models. Honestly full circle haha.

It currently works on these sites with ~70% checkout success rate:

- Walmart - Albertsons - Ocado - Wegmans - FreshDirect - Best Buy - Instacart

Our goal is to hill climb to 90%+ across each.

Test keys are free and run the real flow without placing an order.

New accounts get 10 free completed orders.

https://docs.getagentmall.com/quickstart
